payload.goal: Gate sofar's Tailwind scanner fix on what the host's installed Tailwind can actually parse: @source not landed in 4.1, so emitting it on 4.0.x breaks the build doctor --fix set out to protect.

payload.because: `@source not` landed in Tailwind 4.1 — verified by unpacking both tarballs (the `not ` prefix is parsed only in 4.1.0's dist, absent in 4.0.17) and reproduced live: on real 4.0.17 the inserted line fails the build with "Error: `@source` paths must be quoted", because `not` reads as an unquoted path. A defense that breaks the build it defends is worse than the hazard, so the fix must never be written on a version that cannot parse it, and an ambiguous range must resolve conservatively (`^4` guarantees only 4.0). Auto-adding `source(...)` was rejected because narrowing the scan base silently stops scanning templates outside it — a content-loss edit, not the safe deterministic repair --fix is scoped to (D-P10/BD54); it is offered as a hint the user applies. Severity stays FAIL because the hazard is identical on 4.0; only the repair is withheld.
payload.chose: Version-gate the `@source not` repair on what the host will actually build with: read node_modules/tailwindcss's version when installed, else the declared range's LOWER bound, and write only when that is known >= 4.1. Below it (or when unknowable) doctor still FAILs the hazard but writes nothing, and names the 4.0-compatible remedy — narrowing the import scan base with `source(<dir>)` — computed relative to THAT stylesheet. cssExcludesSofar now also counts a narrowed `source(...)`/`source(none)` as protection.
payload.over: Emitting `@source not` unconditionally on tailwindcss>=4 (the shipped behaviour, which broke a 4.0.17 host's build); trusting the declared range optimistically so `^4` counts as 4.1; auto-rewriting the import to add `source(...)` on pre-4.1 hosts; downgrading the finding to WARN when no fix is available.

payload.text: Tailwind directives sofar emits into a host stylesheet must be checked against the host's INSTALLED version, not just major>=4: `@source not` landed in 4.1 and on 4.0.x fails the build with "Error: `@source` paths must be quoted" (`not` reads as an unquoted path). Establish such a boundary from the artifact, never from memory or a changelog: `npm pack tailwindcss@X`, untar, and grep dist/ for the parse site (`startsWith("not ")` is present in 4.1.0, absent in 4.0.17). Second rule from the same bug: every Tailwind path is resolved relative to the STYLESHEET, so a suggested `source("./src")` becomes src/src for a src/app.css entry — suggestions must be computed per stylesheet like sofarExclusionDirective already is, and live-fired with `npx @tailwindcss/cli -i <entry> -o /dev/null` before shipping.

payload.text: Field observation from building this fix (not acted on here): doctor FAILed this very session as "spans 2 initiatives (torn, live)". The cause is legitimate — the SessionStart hook registered 066e23e9 in writeback-collisions, then start_session was called again with an explicit `initiative`, which start-session.ts documents as a deliberate re-home ("An explicit `initiative` still re-homes deliberately"). The torn-session check cannot tell that deliberate re-home from an accidental branch-flip split, so the sanctioned way to start unmatched work mid-session (sofar new + re-home, protocol clause 2) always trips a FAIL until write-back settles it to history. Worth deciding whether a re-home should emit a marker the check can read.

1.1–2.3: gate the Tailwind scanner fix on the installed version

`sofar doctor --fix` inserted `@source not "…/.sofar";` on any tailwindcss>=4
host. That directive landed in Tailwind 4.1 — on 4.0.x `not` parses as an
unquoted path and the build fails with "Error: `@source` paths must be
quoted", so the defense broke the build it exists to protect (reported from

the hazard is still FAIL (identical on 4.0) but nothing is written and the
hint names the 4.0-compatible remedy: narrowing the import's scan base. That
suggestion is computed per stylesheet, since Tailwind resolves these paths
against the stylesheet — a literal `source("./src")` would mean src/src for a
src/app.css entry. cssExcludesSofar counts a narrowed `source(...)` (or
`source(none)`) as protection, so a repo that applies the hint stops being
flagged.

The 4.1 boundary is established from the artifacts, not memory: the `not `
prefix is parsed in 4.1.0's dist and absent from 4.0.17's. Both paths were
live-fired against real installs — 4.0.17 (nothing written, hint's directive
builds clean) and 4.3.3 under `^4` (fix applied, classes still emit).
